questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly uses inversion to emphasize the adverbial phrase.

A) Only after the rain had stopped did they begin the journey.

B) Only after the rain had stopped they began the journey.

C) Only after the rain had stopped, they began the journey.

D) Only after the rain had stopped then they began the journey.
options: Only after the rain had stopped did they begin the journey.
Only after the rain had stopped they began the journey.
Only after the rain had stopped, they began the journey.
Only after the rain had stopped then they began the journey.
questions.answer: Only after the rain had stopped did they begin the journey.

questions.question:
Which sentence correctly employs a cleft sentence to highlight the specific detail about the meeting time?

A) It was at 3 PM yesterday that we finalized the deal.

B) It was 3 PM yesterday that we finalized the deal.

C) It was yesterday at 3 PM that we finalized the deal.

D) It was yesterday that we finalized the deal at 3 PM.
options: It was at 3 PM yesterday that we finalized the deal.
It was 3 PM yesterday that we finalized the deal.
It was yesterday at 3 PM that we finalized the deal.
It was yesterday that we finalized the deal at 3 PM.
questions.answer: It was yesterday at 3 PM that we finalized the deal.

questions.question:
Select the option that correctly uses the subjunctive mood to express a hypothetical condition.

A) If I were you, I would have taken the job.

B) If I was you, I would have taken the job.

C) If I had been you, I would have taken the job.

D) If I am you, I would have taken the job.
options: If I were you, I would have taken the job.
If I was you, I would have taken the job.
If I had been you, I would have taken the job.
If I am you, I would have taken the job.
questions.answer: If I were you, I would have taken the job.

questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly demonstrates ellipsis, where the word 'they' is omitted but implied.

A) John likes coffee, but not Mary.

B) John likes coffee, but Mary not.

C) John likes coffee, but Mary does not.

D) John likes coffee, but not Mary does.
options: John likes coffee, but not Mary.
John likes coffee, but Mary not.
John likes coffee, but Mary does not.
John likes coffee, but not Mary does.
questions.answer: John likes coffee, but not Mary.

questions.question:
Which sentence uses formal register appropriately in a context discussing a proposal?

A) I think that might be a good idea.

B) It is my opinion that this approach is effective.

C) Frankly, I don't see the benefit.

D) Personally, I believe we should reconsider.
options: I think that might be a good idea.
It is my opinion that this approach is effective.
Frankly, I don't see the benefit.
Personally, I believe we should reconsider.
questions.answer: It is my opinion that this approach is effective.
